شَاصٍ ; fem. شَاصِيَةٌ, pl. of the latter شَاصِيَاتٌ and شَوَاصٍ; part. n. of 1 (S, TA) as said of the eyes [i. e. Fixedly open, or being raised, &c.]: (TA:) and of a water-skin, meaning Filled, or inflated, so that its legs are raised; and of a wine-skin, meaning filled, so that its legs are raised: and of a corpse, meaning Inflated, &c. (S, TA.) It is said in a prov., “إِذَا ٱرْجَحَنَّ شَاصِيًا فَٱرْفَعْ يَدَا
” [expl. in art. رجحن, q. v.]. (S, TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
